column1: # Game profile of Super Mario RPG (Switch, update 1.0.1 = v65536). Plays on the Mac
# Format: see dm/games/README.md; bring-up and measurements in README.md beside this file

# Unity 2021.3.15f1 (IL2CPP) with CRIWARE, SDK 14.3.1, NVN; subsdk0 is the movie module. The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the UnityFS bundles under Data/, plus the player's GLSLC outputs in main
# The game asks for present interval 1 and presents at 60 fps

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)

# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true. The game sets no heap, and with the hardware pool the heap check's alias region reached +4.27 GB of 4.38 GB within its first seconds.

# The layout of Cult of the Lamb and SUPER ROBOT WARS Y: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region), chosen by the NSP script's heap check
# The game calls nvnDeviceSetDepthMode(near = 0) (log: "depth mode near=0"), so its vertex shaders use the main0_z entries; the pipeline bases made before it runs are made for that mode
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader and ComputeShader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# everything with shaders is under Data/: the player's serialized files and the StreamingAssets bundles
